solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: No end of stress amid awful earful

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept
something awful is in a bad state, so the word's letters are badly jumbled
amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the final letter of stress
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone under constant stress gets an awful earful from a nagging voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The S goes into the rearranged EARFUL: REFU-S-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a negative reply, the noun counterpart of saying no.

clue.text: Mostly rosy and in the pink in New Mexico city

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
in the pink means in good health; and simply joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: Someone describes looking rosy-cheeked and healthy on a trip to New Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: Roswell is the New Mexico town famous for a supposed 1947 UFO crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Roswell is a city in New Mexico, so the answer is an instance of the place described.

clue.text: Comedy clubs putting on food

indicators.note: putting something on is placing it into position, here into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: fare is food, as on a menu
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Comedy clubs serving food to their audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is a broad comedy built on absurd situations.

clue.text: I seem to upset when ringing married ex

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order
ringing means forming a circle round, so the other piece sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they get upset whenever they phone a former spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' looks like a phone call to the ex, but it puts M inside the rearranged letters; 'to' is both fodder and part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometime as an adjective means former, as in a sometime professor, which is what ex means.

clue.text: Hilarity initially left old Liberal zonked

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: An old Liberal politician is left exhausted by a fit of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Zonked is slang for exhausted or intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolz is internet slang for fun or laughs, from LOL, laugh out loud.

clue.text: Very good values felons found in craft?

blocks.note: pi is crossword shorthand for pious, very good
rates are values or prices

explanation.surface: Sounds like a review praising the values of criminals who have taken up crafts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like handicraft, but it means boats; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates are sea robbers, criminals operating aboard ships, which are craft.

clue.text: Is determined to be a cut above others ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so each of the two words gives its last letter

blocks.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
to sever is to cut
the last letter of above
the last letter of others

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to end up a cut above everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cut above' is a stock phrase meaning superior; it has to be split into 'a' and 'cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who perseveres keeps going doggedly, which is what being determined means.

clue.text: Spicy soup, bit of rocket for its topping

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its first letter
replacing a top means swapping the first letter for another

blocks.note: the first letter of rocket
bisque is a rich shellfish soup

explanation.surface: A spicy soup gets a garnish of rocket leaves on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket is the salad leaf (arugula in the US). The R takes the place of the B at the top of the soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué means slightly indecent, a common figurative sense of spicy.

clue.text: Piped tool about so long?

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are moved into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks how long a piped tool, perhaps a hose, is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' reads as a measurement, but it is the farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is a dated British way of saying goodbye, as is so long.

clue.text: Rough tykes running around church

indicators.note: running suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged
around places these letters on either side of the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Rowdy little kids are running wild around a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A tyke is a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketchy plan or drawing is rough, lacking detail.

clue.text: Credit injected into troubled marbles plant

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order
something injected into another is put inside it

blocks.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A troubled factory making marbles gets an injection of credit to stay afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory with the marbles, but it is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrambler is a climbing plant that sprawls over supports, such as a scrambling rose.

clue.text: With cuts hurting, perhaps did this

definitions.text: With cuts hurting, perhaps did this

indicators.note: a word that cuts another slices into its middle, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
sore means hurting

explanation.surface: Someone nursing painful cuts probably let rip with some bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition while also housing W inside SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Swore means used curses, which is what someone in pain from cuts might well do.

clue.text: Turns out royal's not involved in failures

indicators.note: something not involved in a word is left out of it

blocks.note: R is short for royal, as in RN
rejects are failed items, cast-offs

explanation.surface: A royal reportedly took no part in some failed ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the R from REJECTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to throw or turn out, as a bouncer does to troublemakers.

clue.text: State case for refugee community

indicators.note: a case is the outside shell, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of refugee
the public is the community at large

explanation.surface: A government argues the case for welcoming a refugee community.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state or nation governed without a monarch.

clue.text: Perhaps the final part in a history period

definitions.text: Perhaps the final part in a history

blocks.clueFragment: Perhaps the final part in a history
blocks.note: first meaning: the conclusion of a tale, of which a history is one kind; also the last five letters of history
second meaning: the US exclamation that closes an argument, like the British full stop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' looks like a span of history beside the first part, but it is the closing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to end discussion, as period or full stop is, and literally names the ending of a narrative.

clue.text: Fancy thinker and Milliband being in agreement!

blocks.note: to fancy is to like
a mind is a thinker, as in great minds
Ed Miliband, former leader of the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to find a thinker they admire agreeing with Ed Miliband.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party from 2010 to 2015; the clue spells his name with two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Like-minded people share the same opinions, so they are in accord with each other.

clue.text: One may take issue with rising fish stocks

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, from bottom to top
stocks means keeps inside, as a shop stocks goods

blocks.note: and means with or plus
a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: Someone may quarrel over rising fish stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take issue' reads as disagree; issue here means children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so someone who takes a child away by force is an abductor of issue.

clue.text: Active ingredient in crisp Ryvitas

indicators.note: an ingredient is a part contained in something, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Reads like a label listing an active ingredient in a crispbread.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryvita is a British brand of rye crispbread; 'Active ingredient' is a phrase from medicine labels, split here.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone lively and nimble, especially for their age.

clue.text: Muse over bad rockets in Canaveral?

indicators.note: something that rockets shoots upwards, and in a down clue going up reads the letters backwards
in places the reversed piece inside the place name

blocks.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ill means bad, as in ill effects
Cape Canaveral in Florida; Canaveral is an example of a cape

explanation.surface: Someone ponders failed rocket launches at Cape Canaveral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse over' reads as ponder, but Muse is the definition and over gives a letter; 'rockets' fits the space scene yet is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over epic poetry.

clue.text: Pop's flipping repetitive nowadays!

indicators.note: repetitive says the piece is used twice in a row
flipping something turns it end to end

blocks.note: AD, anno domini, the present era, written twice

explanation.surface: A child complains that Dad keeps repeating himself these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild swear, but it turns ADAD round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada is a child's word for father, just as pop is an informal one.

clue.text: Let down lad with feet in need of treatment

indicators.note: something in need of treatment is not in proper shape, so its letters must be reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy with sore feet needs a doctor and feels let down.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate a tyre or balloon is to let it down by releasing the air.

clue.text: Say more than enough on foreign exchange

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece put on another is placed after it, so the plentiful word comes second

blocks.note: forex is the usual short form of foreign exchange
ample means plentiful

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have more than enough currency for a trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the plentiful piece after the currency piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Say is used to introduce an instance, exactly as for example does.

clue.text: He's one to have English mild sans head

indicators.note: sans is French for without, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
clement means mild, of weather

explanation.surface: A man orders a pint of English mild, minus the froth.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild is a British dark, low-strength beer, and head is its froth, but neither sense applies. He is helium's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the chemical symbol for helium, which is one of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Join strike, save Grand Hotel!

indicators.note: save means except, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: to strike is to attack
a grand is a thousand, abbreviated K
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Workers urged to join a strike to save the Grand Hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' reads as rescue, but means except: take K from ATTACK and add H.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach is to fasten or join one thing to another.

clue.text: Fault that's spoiled one's time in Galway?

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so its letters are messed about

blocks.note: taken as written
one is I, and 's is short for is
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A traveller complains that one fault spoiled their time in the Irish city of Galway.
explanation.walkthrough: Galway is not the Irish city here but Sir James Galway, the celebrated Northern Irish flute player.
explanation.definitionFit: James Galway is a famous flute player, an example of the musician named; the question mark signals the example.

clue.text: Claim posh girl backtracks in drink

indicators.note: to backtrack is to go back the way you came, so the word is read from the end
in places the girl inside the drink

blocks.note: gel is how a girl is pronounced in an upper-class accent
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Someone says a well-to-do girl went back on her word over drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gel' mimics the plummy English pronunciation of girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, a synonym of claim.

clue.text: Strange way to describe Prince Charles, say!

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving one that is spelt differently

blocks.note: Prince Charles was long the heir to the throne, so heir-like, said with a dropped H

explanation.surface: Jokes about an odd way of describing the then Prince Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Charles, now King Charles III, was heir to the British throne for decades; the invented word heiry suits him.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, uncanny.

clue.text: Do in revolutionary dictator? Fantastic

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the following words
a revolution turns something round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Asks whether a revolutionary dictator is any good, and answers that he is fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A do, short for hairdo, is a hairstyle, and an Afro is a rounded, bushy one.

clue.text: Top record-holding Norwegian band

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the band's name wraps round the record

blocks.note: a-ha, the Norwegian pop band of Take On Me
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A Norwegian band holds the top record in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holding' reads as a single compound, but record is the piece and holding the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first Greek letter, so it means first or top, as in alpha male.

clue.text: Rotten dessert? A slice may put one thus

definitions.text: A slice may put one thus

blocks.note: food that has gone off is rotten
dessert is an example of a course in a meal

explanation.surface: A slice of a rotten dessert could put anyone off their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slice' sits with dessert as a portion, but it is the golf shot that curves the ball wide.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliced golf shot veers sharply sideways, sending a ball or a player away from the intended line.

clue.text: Labour leader blocking blue material

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the first letter is kept
something blocking a passage sits inside it

blocks.note: the first letter of Labour
blue and earthy both describe crude, bawdy humour

explanation.surface: A Labour leader blocks the release of some Tory campaign material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' looks like a party figure such as the one in 14 across, but it is only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly and material both mean belonging to the physical world rather than the spiritual.

clue.text: Public housing unlimited near gorge

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundary letters, so only the inside remains
housing something means giving it a home inside

blocks.note: overt means open, done in public
near with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Reads like a planning note about public housing on unlimited land near a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a canyon next to near, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself with food, which is to overeat.
